name: Joash
description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: But Jehosheba took Joash, the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king's sons that were slain, and hid him and his nurse in the house of the Lord six years. They had to hide that little boy, cuz this is how wicked women are: to stay in power, they'll destroy the men.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: Jehosheba, sister of Ahaziah, took the infant Joash and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being slain, hiding him in the house of the Most High for six years while Athaliah reigned.

note.label: 2 Kings 11: The Hidden King and the Covenant to Be the Lord's People

points: Joash was brought to the throne, the people rejoiced, the city was quiet, and he was seven years old when he began to reign.

note.label: 2 Kings 11: The Hidden King and the Covenant to Be the Lord's People

points: Jehoash began to reign in the seventh year of Jehu and reigned forty years in Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Kings 12: Repairing the House and Dealing Faithfully

points: Jehoash ordered that all the dedicated money brought into the house be gathered by the priests to repair the breaches of the house.

note.label: 2 Kings 12: Repairing the House and Dealing Faithfully

points: Jehoash called Jehoiada and the priests, asked why the house was not repaired, and directed that the money no longer be received by them but delivered directly for the repairs.

note.label: 2 Kings 12: Repairing the House and Dealing Faithfully

points: Jehoash took the hallowed things dedicated by the former kings, and the gold from the treasures, and sent them to Hazael, who then went away.

note.label: 2 Kings 12: Repairing the House and Dealing Faithfully

points: His own servants made a conspiracy and slew Joash in the house of Millo, and Amaziah his son reigned in his place.

note.label: 2 Kings 12: Repairing the House and Dealing Faithfully

points: Amaziah lived fifteen years after the death of Jehoash, and a conspiracy was made against him in Jerusalem so that he fled to Lachish and was slain there.

note.label: 2 Kings 14: Amaziah, the Imperfect Heart, and Jeroboam II

points: Jeroboam the son of Joash, Jeroboam II, began to reign over Israel and reigned forty-one years, doing evil and not departing from the sins of the first Jeroboam.

note.label: 2 Kings 14: Amaziah, the Imperfect Heart, and Jeroboam II

points: But Jehoshabeath the daughter of king Jehoram, wife of Jehoiada the priest and sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah and stole him from among the king's sons that were slain, hiding him and his nurse in a bedchamber.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 22: Ahaziah and the Rise of Athaliah

points: Joash was seven years old when he began to reign and reigned forty years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

points: Joash did that which was right in the sight of the Most High all the days of Jehoiada the priest, because that is what he was taught.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls

points: The Syrians came with a small company, yet the Most High delivered a very great host of Judah into their hand, because Judah had forsaken the Most High God of their fathers; so judgment was executed on Joash for killing Zechariah.

Joash began by doing right under Jehoiada's guidance, repairing the house and clearing out the idols, but none of that was remembered in the end because of the wickedness he turned to after being warned.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 24: Joash Repairs the House and Then Falls
